text: add capability of signing in if a nip07 is detected -- if the user is signed-in allow the user to create highlights on essays NIP-84; load highlights and mark them up in the text of the essay in a very polished way like medium does [...] - **Highlights**: signed-in users select text → "Highlight" pill → publishes a NIP-84 (`kind:9802`) event tagged to the essay's canonical URL, wrapped locally right away (optimistic, doesn't wait on relay confirmation). [...] - **Reading**: on load, subscribes for existing highlights on that URL from four public relays and marks up matching text in place, with a hover tooltip showing who highlighted it and when. [...] Assistant: **Fixed and verified.** The bug you hit — clicking "Highlight" doing nothing, not even prompting a signature — was a real DOM race: the global `mouseup` listener that opens the toolbar wasn't ignoring mouseup events that landed on the toolbar itself, so clicking it destroyed-and-recreated the button mid-click, which silently suppresses the browser's `click` event on the now-detached original element. Added a guard (`f7z.io/src/highlights.js`) so the listener ignores mouseup events originating inside `.n-hl-toolbar`, rebuilt `js/highlights.js`, and re-ran the full flow in a real browser with a fake NIP-07 provider: sign-in → select text → click Highlight → `<mark class="n-highlight">` appears wrapping the selection → hover tooltip shows the highlighter's name/npub and timestamp. All confirmed working. [...] User: for the highlights... don't r-tag the present URL (it's localhost!) use what will be the canonical "a" tag: 30023:fa984bd7dbb282f07e16e7ae87b26a2a7b9b90b7246a44771f0cf5ae58018f52:<d-tag-slug> --- and you should be using that same filter to load existing highlights, like for the attention essay it would be: kinds:[9802], "#a": ["30023:fa984bd7dbb282f07e16e7ae87b26a2a7b9b90b7246a44771f0cf5ae58018f52:attention"] [...] 1. **Anchoring**: highlights now tag a stable NIP-33 `a` reference (`30023:<pubkey>:<slug>`, e.g. `30023:fa98...52:attention`) instead of the literal page URL — no more `r` tags pointing at `localhost`, and it'll keep working correctly across preview deploys, `www` vs bare domain, etc. Both the publish path and the load/subscribe filter use it. Slug is derived from the URL path (`attention`, `memory`, etc.), pubkey is hardcoded to the site's own identity (same one `api/nip05.js` resolves). [...] 2. **Contrast**: the near-unreadable highlight text was the browser's default `<mark>` UA style forcing `color: black`, clashing with light-on-dark essay text. Added `color: inherit` — confirmed now rendering as cream text with a subtle orange underline stroke, not a filled block.
